claims.claim: Qualcomm is extending an edge-compute/mobile silicon and software position into automotive, IoT and data-center/custom-silicon workloads; 28% combined Automotive/IoT growth provides evidence that diversification is already occurring outside handsets.

The structural thesis is resilient only if Qualcomm can reuse compute, connectivity and AI software capabilities across end markets while custom silicon, automotive design wins and IoT scale faster than handset dependence declines; memory/supply constraints and competing silicon architectures are successor bottlenecks/substitutes.

risks.risk: Diversification can be slowed by handset concentration, memory/supply constraints and customer substitution toward competing or in-house silicon.

unknowns.unknown: Durability and incremental margin of the new data-center/custom-silicon ramp remain unproven in current evidence.

claims.claim: The FY2029 $40B non-handset target is a measurable diversification objective rather than current proof; the thesis weakens if automotive, IoT and custom-silicon ramps fail to outgrow handset dependence or if substitutes capture those workloads.
Current 28% Automotive/IoT growth argues against treating diversification as merely narrative, but the evidence does not yet establish data-center/custom-silicon durability or margins.

risks.risk: Customer in-house silicon, competing architectures, handset concentration and supply constraints can reduce diversification value capture.

unknowns.unknown: Segment-level incremental margins and durable data-center shipment economics are not established in reused evidence.
